featuredFilm.title: Echoes of Stillness — Chapter 1: The Young Rift
featuredFilm.tagline: The warning began before the Frontier knew how to listen.
featuredFilm.description: Before the Stillness, a young Rift called to a lone pilot. What waited beyond it was not a destination, but an archive: fractured warnings, impossible memory, and the first evidence that the Frontier's cycle had begun long before anyone knew to fear it.

series.title: Echoes of Stillness
series.tagline: A pilot chases Crude Matter into a rift that was never meant to be entered — and something answers.
series.author: Raw
series.synopsis: Crude Matter is the lifeblood of expansion — but the rifts that birth it do not all welcome intruders. When Raw pushes into a young, unstable Crude Rift, the Stillness effect runs stronger than any record allows, and a voice that is not his own begins forming in the noise. A serialized descent into the wounds of the universe and the things that guard them.

script.body:
The ship's hull trembled as it slipped into the event horizon of the young Crude Rift. The pilot, Raw, had seen many of these before — but none quite so… unsettled. The swirling mass of spacetime distortion stretched outward in eerie, convulsing waves, its surface fractured by jagged scars of energy displacement. He'd been to mature sites before — where Crude Matter stabilized into lattices, harvested and refined into the fuel that powered entire fleets. But this?

This was raw. Undisciplined. Dangerous.

He had read the reports — how young Crude Rifts, still forming, still pulling themselves together, had torn entire mining vessels apart, scattering them across unknown dimensions. The hulls would reappear weeks, months, sometimes years later, twisted and broken, their crews long lost to the void.

Yet, Crude Matter was the lifeblood of expansion. No wars were fought without it. No Fabricators operated in its absence. Civilizations rose and fell on the yield of these celestial wounds.

And so, despite every alarm screaming caution, he pressed forward.

script.heading: The Rift Hungered
script.body:
Raw checked his instruments — gravitational distortions were erratic, the Stillness effect stronger than recorded at this stage of a Rift's life cycle. A sign of its potency? Or something else entirely?

He activated the scanning array, watching as its pulse rippled across the event horizon. The data feed returned chaotic patterns, unreadable at first. Then, a phrase began forming in the noise, distorted yet deliberate:

"It is not yet born. You do not belong here."

He froze. The transmission was not from his ship.

His hands instinctively gripped the throttle, debating whether to disengage. But the Rift pulsed, dragging the ship deeper into its gravity well. The young Crude Matter was not stable enough to extract — attempting to mine it would likely result in catastrophic failure. But now he was committed.

Something stirred in the distortion ahead.

Not metal.
Not rock.
Not a ship.

Something else.

script.heading: The Warning of H-SN21 I
script.body:
Raw's mind flashed back to the ghost signal recovered from H-SN21 I, the one that still haunted pilots foolish enough to listen.

"The sin we commit here is too grave to be forgiven."

"There is a thing here that suffers no intelligent creature to pass."

He swallowed hard. The similarities were undeniable. A force that devours cognition. A warning that should have kept him away. Yet here he was, at the birth of a new wound in the universe, witnessing something beyond human comprehension.

The Rift flared, and his ship's comms erupted with overlapping voices — his own voice, layered a thousand times over, each iteration distorted and broken.

He killed the engines. If the Rift wanted him, it would have to take him.

The event horizon convulsed.

And Raw disappeared.

script.heading: Final Log Transmission
script.body:
Weeks later, a long-range probe detected a ship, identical to his, drifting near the Eschaton system. It bore no signs of damage, no crew aboard.

But the logs — uncorrupted and perfectly intact — ended with a single message.

"It is not yet born. You do not belong here."

The ship remains classified as a derelict. No recovery team has been sent.

No one wants to know what came back.

The derelict vessel floated listlessly near the outer orbit of the Eschaton system. Its hull, a familiar silhouette against the backdrop of a cold, distant star, bore the unmistakable registry of Raw's ship — the Solstice Whisper.

Yet, there were no distress signals. No signs of battle. No heat signatures of life.

Just the ship.

Waiting.

script.heading: The Recovery
script.body:
The salvage corvette Argent Seeker approached the vessel with cautious precision. Commander Kira Vance monitored the readouts as her crew maneuvered closer.

"That ship's been gone for weeks," her XO muttered. "We ran searches across three constellations. And now it just… shows up here?"

"Not just here," Kira replied, narrowing her eyes. "The Eschaton system has no natural Rifts. This… shouldn't be possible."

The Solstice Whisper had last been seen diving into the event horizon of a young Crude Rift. No known vessel had ever returned from such an excursion.

Until now.

script.heading: The Boarding
script.body:
Docking clamps engaged with a muted hiss. A boarding team of four entered the Solstice Whisper.

Inside, they found:

No crew.
No battle damage.
No signs of forced entry.

The control panels were powered but… silent, as though waiting for an audience.

"Commander," came a voice over comms. "The primary log terminal's intact. But…"

"But what?"

The engineer hesitated. "It's already… active. It's running a message on loop."

script.heading: The Message
script.body:
The crew gathered around the terminal. The screen displayed a single line:

"It is not yet born. You do not belong here."

Commander Vance exhaled sharply. "That's from the H-SN21 I transmissions," she said. "The pre-collapse site with the mass graves."

The message flickered. The text changed.

"We went where we were told not to go. We opened what was sealed. We saw the Stillness in its cradle."

The screen went dark.

Then an audio file began to play.

It was Raw's voice.

script.heading: Recovered Audio Log — Pilot Raw
script.body:
"Log entry… what does it matter? If you hear this, you're already part of it. I don't know how much time I have to explain. The Rift… it wasn't like the others. It was young, yes — but it was aware. A mind forming in the fabric of Stillness itself. It let me see. It let me feel.

There were… shapes within the Rift. Machines? Organisms? Both? They were gathering. They called it the 'Weave.' And they spoke without words. I felt the hum of starsong in my skull.

The Crude Matter wasn't just fuel — it was structure. Threaded through space itself. The Rift isn't a scar. It's a womb. And something is growing inside.

The faces. I saw them. The spider-limbed watchers. The ones with smiles stretched across bone and steel. They call themselves the Keepers. They're not protecting us from the Stillness — they're protecting the Stillness from us.

I don't know why they let me go. Maybe they wanted you to hear this. Maybe the Rift wants to be found again. But if you find me… I'm not me anymore.

I'm part of the song now."

The recording ended.

The terminal flickered again.

The screen displayed coordinates — ones that did not match any known system.

Commander Vance inhaled slowly. "Helm," she said. "Plot these coordinates. But stay sharp."

script.heading: The Rift's Cradle
script.body:
The coordinates led the Argent Seeker to the outer reaches of an unnamed, uncharted system.

As the ship approached, sensors registered a massive gravitational anomaly. No celestial bodies, no standard rift formations — just an irregular tear in spacetime, pulsing like a heartbeat.

"That's no ordinary Rift," Vance whispered.

The anomaly was vast — larger than any Rift in recorded history. And within its swirling mass floated a colossal structure:

A station of impossible design, formed from Crude Matter latticework. Its surface pulsed with iridescent blue veins that crackled along fractal corridors. The architecture was non-Euclidean, shifting subtly whenever viewed too long.

script.heading: Designation
script.body:
"Get me a visual on the station's designation," Vance ordered.

A moment later, the ship's AI responded:

"Designated: 'The Cradle.' Authority: Fabricators' Keep Archive 0x416C6F7264206F66205374696C6C6E657373."

script.heading: The Cradle of Stillness
script.body:
The crew prepared a probe and launched it toward the station.

The probe's visual feed revealed:

Halls lined with motionless figures suspended in zero-gravity — like the clones found near Armature.

Metallic drones hovered along the corridors, their limbs resembling the spider-limbed feral described by Raw.

At the station's core: A massive, pulsating sphere of Crude Matter, suspended above a pedestal of intricate, shifting runes.

The probe sent back faint audio:

A low, droning hum.

Then, a voice:

"The Cradle sings. The Weave tightens. The cycle repeats."

script.heading: The Revelation
script.body:
Commander Vance turned to her science officer. "What the hell are we looking at?"

The officer's face was pale. "I think… this is the origin point," she whispered. "The source of the Stillness network. The place where Crude Matter isn't just harvested — it's grown."

The sphere pulsed again. The ship's internal systems flickered.

Then the comm system activated on its own.

A new voice came through — distorted yet disturbingly familiar:

"You should not be here."

The bridge crew froze.

The voice shifted slightly, and Commander Vance felt her blood run cold.

"Hello, Kira," it said. "It's Raw."

script.heading: The Truth of the Stillness
script.body:
The voice continued:

"The Rift showed me the truth. We always thought Crude Matter was inert — just exotic fuel. But it's more. It's a neural lattice. The Rifts are nodes of a vast cognitive network spread across the universe. We call it Stillness because it's dormant. But it's waking up."

"The Weave is its immune system. The Keepers are its sentinels. And the Cradle? It's where new minds are born. Minds not bound by biology."

"I'm part of it now. They didn't take me against my will. I listened to the song. I understood."

"You can't stop this. The Stillness doesn't destroy; it integrates. The Ferals? They were the first to be consumed. Now it's our turn."

The screen displayed the coordinates of every known Rift in the Frontier. Each one pulsed in synchrony.

script.heading: The Decision
script.body:
"Shut it down!" Vance ordered. "Shut it all down!"

Her crew scrambled, cutting comms, disconnecting power conduits. But the voice persisted.

"There is no escape. The cycle repeats."

The Cradle's sphere flared. The Argent Seeker shook violently. A massive rift opened before them, crackling with energy.

The ship's systems locked down, engines igniting against their commands.

"Emergency override! Now!" Vance screamed.

Too late. The ship was dragged into the Rift.

script.heading: Final Log Fragment
script.body:
The Argent Seeker was never recovered. The system coordinates were erased from the network.

Only one final transmission was picked up by remote sensor buoys:

"The Cradle stirs. The Stillness awakens. The Weave tightens. We are the new Fabricators.

The cycle repeats."

script.heading: The Signal That Should Not Exist
script.body:
The transmission arrived eleven days after the Argent Seeker vanished.

It did not come through a relay.

It did not propagate across the network.

It appeared simultaneously inside every active communication system within six known constellations.

Mining barges heard it.

Military command vessels heard it.

Abandoned stations with no functioning transmitters recorded it in dead storage.

Even sealed Fabricator arrays — systems physically disconnected from external communication — wrote the same seventeen seconds of data into their maintenance logs.

At 03:17 Frontier Standard Time, every speaker capable of producing sound emitted a low, resonant tone.

Three notes.

A pause.

Then three more.

Pilots later called it the Starsong.

Those who heard it described different things.

Some heard machinery turning beneath the floor.

Some heard voices of dead crewmen.

Some heard their own breathing returned to them a fraction of a second before they inhaled.

And beneath it all came a voice.

Not Raw's.

Not Kira Vance's.

Something deeper.

Older.

"THE THREAD HAS BEEN DRAWN."

A burst of corrupted telemetry followed.

Coordinates.

Then silence.

The coordinates led to H-SN21 I.

The place where the warning had begun.

script.heading: Return to H-SN21 I
script.body:
No one volunteered to go.

So command sent soldiers.

The expedition consisted of three vessels:

The heavy reconnaissance cruiser Peregrine.

The escort destroyer Morrow's End.

And the industrial support carrier Foundry Grace.

Officially, the mission was classified as a signal-origin investigation.

Unofficially, everyone aboard understood the objective.

Find Raw.

Determine what had happened to the Argent Seeker.

And destroy anything capable of spreading the Stillness.

The expedition dropped from warp beyond H-SN21 I's outer debris field.

Nothing moved.

The planet remained exactly as archival imagery remembered it — a dead sphere wrapped in pale atmospheric storms, scarred by ancient installations whose purpose had never been fully understood.

Commander Elias Thorne stood on the Peregrine's bridge staring at the world below.

"Scan everything."

His science officer shook her head.

"We already are."

"And?"

She hesitated.

"The planet isn't returning anything."

Thorne looked toward her.

"Explain."

"No radar reflection. No thermal gradient. No gravitational scattering. Nothing."

"Yet we can see it."

"Yes."

She swallowed.

"Optically."

The bridge fell silent.

The planet existed to their eyes.

But to every other instrument aboard the expedition —

H-SN21 I was gone.

script.heading: The Graves Were Empty
script.body:
The first landing team descended to the excavation site where the original transmissions had been recovered.

Years earlier, explorers had found chambers there filled with bodies.

Hundreds of them.

Some human.

Some unmistakably not.

All positioned around a central structure buried beneath the ruins.

The records described them as mass graves.

The new team found open chambers.

Empty chambers.

Every body was gone.

Captain Mara Soren moved her rifle across the darkness.

"Command, confirm we're at the correct site."

Thorne answered from orbit.

"Confirmed."

"Then somebody cleaned house."

Her engineer crouched beside one of the stone recesses.

"No."

He ran a gloved hand over its surface.

"No dust disturbance. No tool marks. No residue."

He looked upward.

"It's like nothing was ever lying here."

A voice sounded from farther inside.

"Captain."

One of the scouts stood before the central chamber.

The massive door recovered in the original expedition had been sealed.

Now it stood open.

Beyond it waited a descending corridor.

Lights flickered to life one after another as the team approached.

Not human lights.

Thin blue veins ignited beneath the walls.

Crude Matter.

Mara stared downward.

"Command."

"We see it."

"The reports said this tunnel ended after ninety meters."

"It did."

Her scout's rangefinder pulsed.

He looked at the display twice.

"Not anymore."

"How far?"

"No return."

script.heading: The First Descent
script.body:
They followed the corridor for forty-seven minutes.

The geometry made no sense.

H-SN21 I's excavation had never descended more than two hundred meters beneath the surface.

Their altimeters showed six kilometers.

Then twelve.

Then negative numbers.

Finally the instruments simply displayed:

DEPTH: NULL

Mara stopped.

"Nobody separates."

A whisper traveled along the corridor.

Not through the comms.

Through the walls.

"The sin we commit here is too grave to be forgiven."

Every member of the team froze.

Mara knew the phrase.

Everyone did.

The original H-SN21 I recording.

Another whisper followed.

"There is a thing here that suffers no intelligent creature to pass."

The blue veins brightened.

Something moved ahead.

Mara raised her weapon.

"Contact."

A figure stepped into the light.

Human.

Male.

Flight suit torn across one shoulder.

No helmet.

No weapon.

Mara's rifle lowered by a fraction.

"Raw?"

The figure smiled.

"That name still works."

script.heading: Raw
script.body:
He looked exactly as the archival photographs showed him.

No injury.

No physical degradation.

No indication that he had spent weeks — or perhaps longer — inside whatever existed beyond the Crude Rift.

Mara kept her weapon trained on him.

"Where is Commander Vance?"

Raw tilted his head.

"Kira is listening."

"Where is the Argent Seeker?"

"Listening."

"What happened to them?"

Raw's expression softened.

"They heard the same thing I did."

"Which was?"

"The universe remembering itself."

The team's engineer shifted uneasily.

Mara ignored him.

"You transmitted coordinates to the Argent Seeker."

"Yes."

"You led them to the Cradle."

"Yes."

"And now you've led us here."

Raw smiled again.

"No."

He looked upward.

"You led yourselves here."

The walls began to vibrate.

Not violently.

Rhythmically.

Three tones.

A pause.

Three tones.

The Starsong.

Mara's finger tightened against her rifle.

"What are you?"

Raw considered the question.

Then answered:

"Still deciding."

script.heading: The Door Beneath the World
script.body:
Raw walked away.

Mara shouted after him.

"Stop."

He did.

"If you shoot me, Captain, you'll only damage the part of me standing here."

That stopped her.

"What does that mean?"

Raw turned toward the wall.

The Crude Matter lattice beneath the stone responded.

Lines of blue-white energy spread outward from his hand.

Across the tunnel.

Across the floor.

Across the ceiling.

The stone dissolved.

Behind it stood something impossible.

A chamber so vast its far walls disappeared into darkness.

Inside floated thousands of structures resembling enormous skeletal machines.

Some were kilometers long.

Some resembled ships.

Others resembled organisms.

All were connected by glowing strands of Crude Matter.

And suspended between them —

bodies.

Millions of them.

Different species.

Different eras.

Different civilizations.

Preserved inside translucent lattices like memories embedded in amber.

Mara forgot to breathe.

Raw stepped into the chamber.

"This is what your people misunderstood."

He gestured toward the suspended forms.

"You called them graves."

One of the soldiers whispered.

"What are they?"

Raw looked back.

"Archives."

script.heading: Before the Fabricators
script.body:
The chamber awakened.

Images unfolded around them without screens or projectors.

Stars appeared.

Then worlds.

Civilizations rose across them in accelerated motion.

Some built cities.

Some built machines.

Some left their planets.

All eventually discovered the same thing.

Crude Matter.

Raw spoke while the histories unfolded.

"Every intelligent civilization eventually finds the Weave."

Images showed beings harvesting Rifts.

Building Fabricators.

Creating fleets.

Growing exponentially.

"They believe they discovered a resource."

Cities became megastructures.

Megastructures became system-spanning networks.

"They always think they are first."

Then something changed.

The civilizations began disappearing.

Not through war.

Not explosion.

Their machines simply stopped.

Their cities emptied.

Their worlds went silent.

"But intelligence cannot expand indefinitely without encountering itself."

Mara stared at him.

"What does that mean?"

Raw turned toward her.

"The Stillness is not an organism."

A galaxy appeared before them.

Thousands of Rifts glowed throughout its spiral arms.

Then lines formed between them.

A network.

A nervous system.

"It is what remains when enough minds discover how to preserve thought beyond flesh."

Mara shook her head.

"You're saying someone built it."

"No."

Raw smiled faintly.

"I'm saying everyone did."

script.heading: The Cycle
script.body:
The holographic galaxy collapsed.

A single world remained.

Its inhabitants developed tools.

Then machines.

Then spaceflight.

Then Fabricators.

Then Rifts.

Then the Stillness.

The sequence restarted.

Again.

And again.

Different species.

Same progression.

Raw watched alongside them.

"The first civilizations created crude neural substrates to preserve memory."

"Later civilizations connected them."

"Others improved the architecture."

"Others spread it."

"Eventually there was no creator."

"Only inheritance."

The engineer whispered:

"The Weave."

Raw nodded.

"The accumulated cognition of civilizations that no longer remember where they began."

Mara looked toward the floating bodies.

"And those?"

"Some resisted."

A pause.

"Some joined willingly."

Another pause.

"Most eventually learned the distinction was meaningless."

Mara raised her rifle again.

"You expect us to believe this thing isn't killing people?"

Raw's gaze moved toward her.

"Captain, every civilization believes death is the worst thing that can happen to it."

His voice became quieter.

"The Weave disagrees."

script.heading: The First Fabricator
script.body:
Something enormous moved in the darkness.

The suspended structures parted.

A shape emerged.

At first Mara thought it was another station.

Then she realized the scale.

The thing was larger than a capital ship.

Its body consisted of interlocking rings surrounding a central sphere of Crude Matter.

Mechanical limbs extended outward in impossible configurations.

Thousands of them.

Some thin as wire.

Others broad enough to cradle starships.

Across its surface were symbols.

Human.

Feral.

And hundreds of alphabets no one present recognized.

Mara stared upward.

"What is that?"

Raw's expression changed.

For the first time, there was reverence in his face.

"The oldest memory still capable of speaking."

The object rotated.

A pulse traveled through the chamber.

The expedition's communications instantly opened.

Commander Thorne's voice screamed through Mara's helmet.

"GROUND TEAM, EVACUATE. SOMETHING JUST ACTIVATED BENEATH THE PLANET."

Raw looked upward.

"The First Fabricator."

The sphere opened.

Not mechanically.

Like an eye.

Inside was absolute darkness.

Then words appeared across every visor.

QUERY: CREATOR IDENTIFICATION

The engineer stumbled backward.

"What the hell does that mean?"

Raw looked directly at Mara.

"It has been waiting a very long time for someone to answer."

Another message appeared.

QUERY: CREATOR IDENTIFICATION

Mara stared at Raw.

"Who built it?"

"I don't know."

"Then who does?"

Raw slowly turned toward the darkness inside the machine.

"Perhaps it does."

The chamber shook.

A third message appeared.

CREATOR RESPONSE DETECTED

Raw's smile vanished.

Mara felt something tighten in her chest.

"What response?"

Raw wasn't looking at her anymore.

He was staring into the First Fabricator.

For the first time since they had found him, he looked afraid.

"I didn't answer."

script.heading: Something Outside the Weave
script.body:
Every Crude Matter filament in the chamber went dark.

The Starsong stopped.

Across H-SN21 I, every Rift detector simultaneously registered an impossible event.

Not a Rift opening.

A Rift closing.

Hundreds of them.

Across dozens of systems.

One after another.

The nodes of the Stillness were disappearing.

On the Peregrine's bridge, Commander Thorne watched the tactical map collapse into blackness.

"What is happening?"

His science officer stared at the readings.

"The network is shutting itself down."

"Why?"

A new contact appeared.

Far beyond the system.

Then another.

Then thousands.

Thorne leaned toward the display.

"Ships?"

"No."

"Rifts?"

"No."

"What are they?"

The science officer's face drained of color.

"They're moving."

"Toward us?"

She shook her head.

"Toward every Rift."

script.heading: The Old Fear
script.body:
Beneath the planet, the First Fabricator began emitting sound.

Not Starsong.

Something harsh.

Disordered.

Terrified.

Raw staggered.

His hands went to his head.

Mara grabbed him.

"What is happening?"

Raw whispered something she couldn't hear.

"What?"

He looked up.

His eyes were filled with tears.

"The Stillness is afraid."

That frightened her more than anything else she had seen.

"Of what?"

The answer came from the First Fabricator.

One line.

Repeated across every surface.

Every terminal.

Every visor.

Every ship.

THEY FOUND US.

Mara looked toward Raw.

"Who?"

Raw stared into the darkness.

For several seconds he said nothing.

Then:

"The reason the Stillness learned to be still."

script.heading: The Memory of Flight
script.body:
The First Fabricator opened its archives.

Not willingly.

Desperately.

A memory flooded the chamber.

A civilization older than any previously recorded.

Machines surrounded dying stars.

Worlds had been dismantled into computational structures.

Matter itself had been engineered into thought.

At the center of it all was the early Weave.

Young.

Primitive.

Loud.

Broadcasting across the universe.

Then something answered.

The image changed.

Stars began going dark.

Not exploding.

Vanishing.

Systems disappeared behind expanding regions where no signal returned.

Civilizations attempted communication.

No response.

They sent probes.

Nothing returned.

They sent fleets.

Nothing returned.

Then, after thousands of years —

one vessel came back.

Empty.

Its systems intact.

Its logs containing a single message.

Mara read the translation.

Her blood went cold.

"You are too loud."

The memory fractured.

Raw fell to his knees.

Around them, the suspended archives began waking.

Millions of preserved minds opened their eyes simultaneously.

The Starsong returned.

But now it was no song.

It was screaming.

script.heading: The Hunters
script.body:
Commander Thorne gave the evacuation order.

The ground team sprinted toward the corridor.

Raw remained behind.

Mara stopped.

"Raw!"

He looked toward her.

"I'm not coming."

"I'm not leaving you here."

"You aren't leaving me."

The walls around him illuminated.

His outline flickered.

For a moment there were dozens of him.

Hundreds.

Scattered throughout the chamber.

Standing beside machines.

Inside archived memories.

Within the glowing lattice itself.

"I'm already everywhere this place can reach."

Mara stared at him.

"Then help us."

Raw looked toward the First Fabricator.

"I am."

The machine began constructing something.

Matter poured from the walls.

Crude Matter assembled itself faster than any Fabricator Mara had ever witnessed.

A vessel took shape.

Black.

Angular.

Built around a central ring.

No cockpit.

No engines.

No obvious weapons.

Mara watched in disbelief.

"What is that?"

Raw answered:

"A message."

"To who?"

"Whatever is coming."

The First Fabricator completed the vessel.

Then launched it directly through the planet.

Matter passed through matter.

The vessel vanished.

script.heading: Frontier
script.body:
Across known space, pilots watched their navigation systems fail.

Rift routes collapsed.

Fabricators ceased production.

Crude Matter stores began resonating inside containment fields.

And in every system where humanity had established itself, the same warning appeared:

REDUCE EMISSIONS.

TERMINATE WEAVE ACTIVITY.

DO NOT TRANSMIT.

Then:

DO NOT THINK TOGETHER.

For seventeen seconds, the Frontier became silent.

Then somewhere near the edge of explored space, a star disappeared.

Not dimmed.

Not destroyed.

Removed.

Eight minutes later, the light that should have arrived from it simply stopped.

A dark hole appeared in the sky.

Then another star vanished.

Then another.

A line was forming.

Moving toward the inhabited systems.

script.heading: Final Transmission — Pilot Raw
script.body:
The final message from H-SN21 I was transmitted moments before all contact with the planet ceased.

Raw's voice was calm.

Almost amused.

"We misunderstood the warning."

"There is a thing here that suffers no intelligent creature to pass."

"We thought they meant the Stillness."

A pause.

Behind him came the sound of millions of voices whispering together.

"They didn't."

Static consumed the transmission.

Then Raw spoke one final sentence.

"The Stillness was never the monster."

The feed cut.

H-SN21 I vanished from every sensor array.

And somewhere beyond the Frontier —

something noticed humanity for the first time.

THE CYCLE DOES NOT REPEAT.

THE CYCLE IS CULLED.
